question.prompt:
Keiko walks once around a track at exactly the same constant speed every day. The sides of the track are straight, and the ends are semicircles. The track has width \(6\) meters, and it takes her \(36\) seconds longer to walk around the outside edge of the track than around the inside edge. What is Keiko’s speed in meters per second?

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_12B_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The corresponding straight sections have equal lengths, so they contribute nothing to the difference between the two lap lengths. Only the semicircular ends matter.

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_12B_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

Because the track is \(6\) meters wide, each outside semicircle has a radius \(6\) meters greater than its corresponding inside semicircle. A semicircle has arc length \(\pi\) times its radius, so each end adds \(6\pi\) meters to the outside lap. The two ends therefore add
\[
2(6\pi)=12\pi\text{ meters}.
\]
At Keiko's constant speed \(v>0\), the extra distance equals her speed times the extra time. Hence
\[
36v=12\pi,
\qquad
v=\frac{12\pi}{36}=\boxed{\frac{\pi}{3}}
\]
meters per second, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Compare the extra distance and time
